texts.orig: The presence of midwall late gadolinium enhancement as a marker of myocardial fibrosis was independently assessed by the core laboratory blinded to clinical details. First, the core laboratory assessed each scan for acceptable image quality according to standardized criteria. The presence or absence of midwall late gadolinium enhancement was assessed qualitatively by two experienced readers (MD and RE, RB, KL or NC), and differentiated from the pattern of scarring due to prior myocardial infarction, based upon short axis slices in two-phase encoding directions and long-axis images (Supplement eTable 2). The opinion of a third independent experienced reader was sought for any discordant classifications, and site investigators and attending physicians were blinded to the cardiac magnetic resonance findings other than any unexpected clinically urgent findings.

The opinion of a third independent experienced reader was sought for any discordant classifications, and site investigators and attending physicians were blinded to the cardiac magnetic resonance findings other than any unexpected clinically urgent findings.

texts.orig: D. Details of co-enrolment with the EASY-AS Trial
texts.text: D. Details of co-enrolment with the EASY-AS Trial

texts.label: text
texts.orig: During the recruitment phase of the trial, the EASY-AS trial opened to recruitment, randomizing patients with asymptomatic severe aortic stenosis but not necessarily with myocardial fibrosis, to early aortic valve intervention or guideline-directed conservative management (NCT04204915). The EVOLVED trial permitted co-enrolment with the EASY-AS trial. Patients from EASY-AS who were eligible for EVOLVED took the trial arm allocation from the EASY-AS randomization. The flow of patients through EVOLVED and EASY-AS is shown on the following figure. In total, 47 patients were co-enrolled in the EVOLVED and EASY-AS trials.

texts.orig: One participant who was randomized to early aortic valve intervention was excluded from the modified intention-to-treat analysis. This patient was randomized but subsequently identified to be ineligible because of a referral for aortic valve surgery prior to being approached to participate in the trial.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: A second participant randomized to guideline-directed conservative management was initially randomized in error on the test site rather than the live randomization site. Before they were randomized on the live site, their eligibility was not re-confirmed, but they had developed symptoms and had been referred by another cardiologist for aortic valve intervention. When this was subsequently identified, the patient was withdrawn by the Principal Investigator, without any follow-up being completed. As a result, the patient was also excluded from the modified intention-to-treat analysis.

texts.orig: Recruitment to the trial was halted on 17 March 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic in line with a United Kingdom Government directive. Recruitment to the trial did not fully recover, and the results of the AVATAR and RECOVERY trials suggested a larger treatment effect of early intervention than had been assumed in the original power calculation. A decision to halt recruitment into the trial on the prespecified date of 31 October 2022 was therefore taken by the Trial Steering Committee.
